articles.headline: Reserve Bank of India Revises Basel-III Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) Norms and Expands Unified Lending Interface (ULI)
articles.source_name: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) • Official Releases
executive_brief: Reserve Bank of India Revises Basel-III Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) Norms and Expands Unified Lending Interface (ULI)

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) issued revised Basel-III Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) guidelines assigning higher run-off factors for instant digital retail deposits while expanding the Unified Lending Interface (ULI) digital public infra
Mapped to GS-3 (Economy) for UPSC CSE Prelims & Mains revision.

detailedExplanation: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) issued revised Basel-III Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) guidelines requiring scheduled commercial banks to maintain an additional High-Quality Liquid Assets (HQLA) buffer in Government Securities against instant 24/7 digital banking run-offs. Simultaneously, RBI scaled up the Unified Lending Interface (ULI) architecture, integrating consent-based land records, GST filings, and satellite crop data to reduce rural and MSME credit appraisal times.
Positioned within India’s macroeconomic stability, fiscal-monetary policy coordination, banking regulation, and sustainable infrastructure growth trajectory.

articles.headline: ISRO Conducts Semi-Cryogenic Engine (SCE-200) Hot Test Ahead of Chandrayaan-4 & Cabinet Clears BioE3 Policy
executive_brief: ISRO Conducts Semi-Cryogenic Engine (SCE-200) Hot Test Ahead of Chandrayaan-4 & Cabinet Clears BioE3 Policy

ISRO completed hot-testing of the 2,000 kN thrust SCE-200 semi-cryogenic pre-burner using refined kerosene (RP-1) and liquid oxygen (LOX) for LVM3 payload augmentation, alongside Union Cabinet approval of the BioE3 biomanufacturing policy.
Mapped to GS-2 (Editorials and Opinions) for UPSC CSE Prelims & Mains revision.

detailedExplanation: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) successfully conducted the hot test of its 2,000 kN thrust SCE-200 semi-cryogenic engine pre-burner at the Mahendragiri Propulsion Complex. Utilizing refined kerosene (Isrosene / RP-1) and liquid oxygen (LOX), the stage replaces the core liquid stage of LVM3 to boost Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO) payload capacity for the upcoming Chandrayaan-4 Lunar Sample Return and Bharatiya Antariksha Station missions.
Evaluated within India’s constitutional and statutory governance framework, focusing on institutional checks and balances, parliamentary accountability, and federal coordination.

Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) accelerator mass spectrometry (AMS) carbon dating confirmed Iron Age urbanization along the Porunai (Thamirabarani) river basin dating to 1155 BCE, while India finalized the UNESCO World Heritage nominat
Mapped to GS-1 (Reports, Indices and Government Data) for UPSC CSE Prelims & Mains revision.

articles.headline: Supreme Court 7-Judge Constitution Bench Upholds State Power to Sub-Classify Scheduled Castes Under Article 16(4)
articles.primary_category: Supreme Court Judgments and Important Legal Developments
executive_brief: A 7-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court ruled 6:1 in State of Punjab v.
Davinder Singh that States are constitutionally empowered under Articles 15(4) and 16(4) to sub-classify Scheduled Castes based on empirical data of inadequate representation.
The Court overruled the 2004 E.V.

detailedExplanation: A 7-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court ruled 6:1 in State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh that States are constitutionally empowered under Articles 15(4) and 16(4) to sub-classify Scheduled Castes based on empirical data of inadequate representation.

The Court overruled the 2004 E.V. Chinnaiah judgment which had treated Scheduled Castes as a homogeneous class. The Bench clarified that sub-classification does not tinker with the Presidential Notification under Article 341(1) and requires quantifiable empirical evidence collected by the State.

articles.headline: Premature redemption under Sovereign Gold Bond (SGB) Scheme - Redemption Price for premature redemption of SGB 2019-20 Series VI due on October 30, 2026
articles.source_name: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) • Official Releases
secondary_tags: Growth, Budget, Taxation and Economic Indicators
executive_brief: In terms of GOI notification F.No.

4(7)-B(W&M)/2019 dated September 30, 2019 (SGB 2019-20 Series VI - Issue date October 30, 2019) on Sovereign Gold Bond Scheme, premature redemption of Gold Bond may be permitted after fifth year from the date of issue of such Gold Bond on the date on which interest is payable.
Accordingly, the next due date of premature redemption of the above tranche shall be on October 30, 2026.

detailedExplanation: In terms of GOI notification F.No. 4(7)-B(W&M)/2019 dated September 30, 2019 (SGB 2019-20 Series VI - Issue date October 30, 2019) on Sovereign Gold Bond Scheme, premature redemption of Gold Bond may be permitted after fifth year from the date of issue of such Gold Bond on the date on which interest is payable.

Accordingly, the next due date of premature redemption of the above tranche shall be on October 30, 2026. Further, the redemption price of SGB shall be based on simple average of closing price of gold of 999 purity of previous three business days from the date of redemption, as published by the India Bullion and Jewellers Association Ltd (IBJA). Accordingly, the redemption price for premature redemption due on October 30, 2026, shall be ₹14,213/- (Rupees Fourteen Thousand Two Hundred and Thirteen Only) per unit of SGB based on the simple average of closing price of gold for the three business days i.e., October 27, October 28, and October 29, 2026.

articles.source_name: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) • Official Releases
executive_brief: The Reserve Bank of India issued Directions under Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 to The Irinjalakuda Town Co-operative Bank Ltd., Kerala vide Directive No.

CO.DOS.SED.No.D-01/12-22-350/2025-2026 dated July 29, 2025 for a period of six months up to close of business on January 30, 2026, which was last extended up to close of business on October 30, 2026 vide Directive No.

detailedExplanation: The Reserve Bank of India issued Directions under Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 to The Irinjalakuda Town Co-operative Bank Ltd., Kerala vide Directive No. CO.DOS.SED.No.D-01/12-22-350/2025-2026 dated July 29, 2025 for a period of six months up to close of business on January 30, 2026, which was last extended up to close of business on October 30, 2026 vide Directive No.

DOR.MON.No.D-27/12.26.061/2026-27 dated July 21, 2026. The Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that in the public interest, it is necessary to further extend the period of operation of the Directive beyond close of business on October 30, 2026. Accordingly, the Reserve Bank of India, in the exercise of powers vested in it under sub-section (1) of Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, hereby extends the Directive for a further period of three months from close of business on October 30, 2026, to close of business on January 30, 2027, subject to review.

articles.source_name: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) • Official Releases
executive_brief: Government of India has announced the sale (re-issue) of Government Securities, as detailed below, through auction to be held on October 30, 2026 (Friday).

As per the extant scheme of underwriting commitment notified on November 14, 2007, the amounts of Minimum Underwriting Commitment (MUC) and the minimum bidding commitment under Additional Competitive Underwriting (ACU) auction, applicable to each Primary Dealer (PD), are as under: (₹ crore) Security Notified Amount MUC amount per PD Minimum bidding commitment per PD under ACU auction 6.20% GS 2029 9,000 215 215 6.57% GS 2033 12,000 286 286 7.63% GS 2056 9,000 215 215 7.50% GOI SGrB 2056 3,000 72 72 The underwriting auction will be conducted through multiple price-based method on October 30, 2026 (Friday).
PDs may submit their bids for ACU auction electronically through Reserve Bank of India’s Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system) between 09:00 A.M.

detailedExplanation: Government of India has announced the sale (re-issue) of Government Securities, as detailed below, through auction to be held on October 30, 2026 (Friday). As per the extant scheme of underwriting commitment notified on November 14, 2007, the amounts of Minimum Underwriting Commitment (MUC) and the minimum bidding commitment under Additional Competitive Underwriting (ACU) auction, applicable to each Primary Dealer (PD), are as under: (₹ crore) Security Notified Amount MUC amount per PD Minimum bidding commitment per PD under ACU auction 6.20% GS 2029 9,000 215 215 6.57% GS 2033 12,000 286 286 7.63% GS 2056 9,000 215 215 7.50% GOI SGrB 2056 3,000 72 72 The underwriting auction will be conducted through multiple price-based method on October 30, 2026 (Friday).

PDs may submit their bids for ACU auction electronically through Reserve Bank of India’s Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system) between 09:00 A.M. on the day of underwriting auction. The underwriting commission will be credited to the current account of the respective PDs with RBI on the day of issue of securities.

articles.headline: Directions under Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 – Lokapavani Mahila Sahakari Bank Niyamitha, Mandya - Extension of Period
articles.source_name: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) • Official Releases
executive_brief: The Reserve Bank of India issued Directions under Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 to Lokapavani Mahila Sahakari Bank Niyamitha, Mandya vide Directive No.
BLR.DOS.SSMS.No.S628/09-01-242/2025-2026 dated July 29, 2025, for a period of six months up to close of business on January 30, 2026.
The Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that in the public interest, it is necessary to further extend the period of operation of the Directive beyond close of business on October 30, 2026.

detailedExplanation: The Reserve Bank of India issued Directions under Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 to Lokapavani Mahila Sahakari Bank Niyamitha, Mandya vide Directive No. BLR.DOS.SSMS.No.S628/09-01-242/2025-2026 dated July 29, 2025, for a period of six months up to close of business on January 30, 2026.

The Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that in the public interest, it is necessary to further extend the period of operation of the Directive beyond close of business on October 30, 2026. Accordingly, the Reserve Bank of India, in the exercise of powers vested in it under sub-section (1) of Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, hereby extends the Directive for a further period of three months from close of business on October 30, 2026 to close of business on January 30, 2027, subject to review. The aforesaid extension and /or modification by the Reserve Bank of India should not per-se be construed to imply that the Reserve Bank of India is satisfied with the financial position of the bank.

articles.headline: NITI Aayog & UNDP Release Updated National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) Assessment
articles.source_name: Press Information Bureau (PIB) • Govt of India
executive_brief: NITI Aayog, in collaboration with UNDP and OPHI, released the updated National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) tracking 12 indicators across Health, Education, and Standard of Living.
India’s National MPI adds Maternal Health and Bank Account indicators to the 10 global MPI parameters using the Alkire-Foster methodology.
Steepest declines in deprivation were recorded in sanitation, cooking fuel (PMUY), and rural housing.

detailedExplanation: NITI Aayog, in collaboration with UNDP and OPHI, released the updated National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) tracking 12 indicators across Health, Education, and Standard of Living. India’s National MPI adds Maternal Health and Bank Account indicators to the 10 global MPI parameters using the Alkire-Foster methodology.

Steepest declines in deprivation were recorded in sanitation, cooking fuel (PMUY), and rural housing. Three equally weighted dimensions (1/3 each): Health (Nutrition, Child & Adolescent Mortality, Maternal Health), Education (Years of Schooling, School Attendance), and Standard of Living (7 indicators). Computes both Headcount Ratio (H — proportion of multidimensionally poor) and Intensity of Poverty (A — average share of weighted deprivations).

articles.headline: Election Commission of India Releases Verified Electoral Rolls Post-Special Summary Revision (SIR)
executive_brief: The Election Commission of India (ECI) published verified electoral rolls following Special Summary Revision (SIR), enrolling over 1.4 million new young voters.
Under Section 14(b) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, four qualifying dates (Jan 1, Apr 1, Jul 1, Oct 1) now enable quarterly voter registration.
ERONet de-duplication algorithms and Booth Level Officers (BLOs) purged duplicate and shifted entries across constituencies.

detailedExplanation: The Election Commission of India (ECI) published verified electoral rolls following Special Summary Revision (SIR), enrolling over 1.4 million new young voters. Under Section 14(b) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, four qualifying dates (Jan 1, Apr 1, Jul 1, Oct 1) now enable quarterly voter registration.

ERONet de-duplication algorithms and Booth Level Officers (BLOs) purged duplicate and shifted entries across constituencies. Election Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021 replaced the single January 1 qualifying date with four quarterly qualifying dates under Section 14(b) of RPA 1950. Form 6 is used for new voter registration, Form 7 for deletion/objection, and Form 8 for correction or shifting of residence.

articles.headline: Explained: Meteorological Drivers of Rapid Cyclonic Storm Intensification in the Bay of Bengal
executive_brief: Atmospheric scientists report anomalous Sea Surface Temperatures (SST > 30°C) and high Tropical Cyclone Heat Potential (TCHP) in the Bay of Bengal driving rapid cyclone intensification.
Rapid Intensification (RI) is defined as an increase in maximum sustained winds of at least 30 knots (55 km/h) within 24 hours.
Low vertical wind shear and freshwater stratification from river runoff prevent cooler subsurface water from mixing upward.

detailedExplanation: Atmospheric scientists report anomalous Sea Surface Temperatures (SST > 30°C) and high Tropical Cyclone Heat Potential (TCHP) in the Bay of Bengal driving rapid cyclone intensification. Rapid Intensification (RI) is defined as an increase in maximum sustained winds of at least 30 knots (55 km/h) within 24 hours.

Low vertical wind shear and freshwater stratification from river runoff prevent cooler subsurface water from mixing upward. Bay of Bengal receives massive freshwater influx from Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna rivers, creating a shallow, warm barrier layer. Post-monsoon (October–November) cyclones frequently undergo rapid intensification due to weak vertical wind shear and high mid-tropospheric humidity.

detailedExplanation: The Railway Board sanctioned rapid rollout of Kavach 4.0, India’s indigenous Automatic Train Protection (ATP) system developed by RDSO. Developed indigenously by Research Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO) in collaboration with three Indian OEMs. Safety Integrity Level-4 (SIL-4) implies a probability of dangerous failure of less than 1 in 10,000 years.

articles.headline: Supreme Court Issues Compliance Directives on Section 6A Citizenship Act & Border Fencing in Assam
articles.primary_category: Supreme Court Judgments and Important Legal Developments
executive_brief: Following its 5-Judge Constitution Bench verdict (4:1) upholding Section 6A of the Citizenship Act, 1955, the Supreme Court directed time-bound border fencing and tribunal digitization.
Section 6A gives statutory effect to the 1985 Assam Accord, fixing March 25, 1971 as the cut-off date for citizenship registration in Assam.
The Court held that Parliament possesses plenary legislative competence under Article 11 to enact special citizenship provisions.

detailedExplanation: Following its 5-Judge Constitution Bench verdict (4:1) upholding Section 6A of the Citizenship Act, 1955, the Supreme Court directed time-bound border fencing and tribunal digitization. Section 6A gives statutory effect to the 1985 Assam Accord, fixing March 25, 1971 as the cut-off date for citizenship registration in Assam.

The Court held that Parliament possesses plenary legislative competence under Article 11 to enact special citizenship provisions. Persons who entered Assam before January 1, 1966 were deemed citizens; those entering between Jan 1, 1966 and March 24, 1971 were eligible after a 10-year disenfranchisement period. Those entering on or after March 25, 1971 are declared illegal immigrants to be detected and deported through Foreigners Tribunals.

articles.headline: NTCA High-Level Panel Reviews Project Cheetah Habitat Expansion from Kuno to Gandhi Sagar
secondary_tags: Science Policy, Research Missions and Innovation
executive_brief: The National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) reviewed prey-base augmentation and grassland management connecting Kuno National Park with Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary.
Gandhi Sagar in Mandsaur/Nimach districts (crossed by the Chambal River) is prepared as India’s second cheetah meta-population habitat.
The world’s first intercontinental large carnivore translocation brings African Cheetahs (Acinonyx jubatus) from Namibia and South Africa.

detailedExplanation: The National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) reviewed prey-base augmentation and grassland management connecting Kuno National Park with Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary. Gandhi Sagar in Mandsaur/Nimach districts (crossed by the Chambal River) is prepared as India’s second cheetah meta-population habitat.

The world’s first intercontinental large carnivore translocation brings African Cheetahs (Acinonyx jubatus) from Namibia and South Africa. NTCA is a statutory body under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) constituted under Section 38L of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. African Cheetah is listed as "Vulnerable" on the IUCN Red List, whereas the Asiatic Cheetah (*Acinonyx jubatus venaticus*) is "Critically Endangered" and confined to Iran.

articles.headline: Editorial Analysis: Institutional Autonomy of Constitutional & Statutory Regulatory Watchdogs
executive_brief: Evaluates appointment committees, tenure security, and financial autonomy of constitutional and statutory bodies in light of Anoop Baranwal v.
Union of India and the CEC Act, 2023.
Under the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, the selection panel comprises the Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet Minister, and the Leader of Opposition.

detailedExplanation: Evaluates appointment committees, tenure security, and financial autonomy of constitutional and statutory bodies in light of Anoop Baranwal v. Union of India and the CEC Act, 2023.

Under the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, the selection panel comprises the Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet Minister, and the Leader of Opposition. Highlights the constitutional balance between parliamentary legislative power under Article 324(2) and insulation of umpires from executive dominance. In Anoop Baranwal (2023), a 5-judge SC bench had created an interim committee of PM, LoP, and CJI until Parliament enacted a law under Article 324(2).

executive_brief: Held 6:1 that Article 16(4) empowers States to sub-classify Scheduled Castes for equitable affirmative action, overruling the 2004 E.V.

articles.headline: Supreme Court Issues Directives for Expeditious Border Fencing & Foreigners Tribunal Audits in Assam
executive_brief: The **Supreme Court** issued compliance directives to the **Ministry of Home Affairs** following its verdict upholding **Section 6A of the Citizenship Act, 1955**.
Directives mandate time-bound completion of **Indo-Bangladesh border fencing** and accelerated biometric profiling of migrants from the **1966–1971 stream**.
The bench ordered digitization of **Foreigners Tribunals in Assam** to ensure statutory constitutionality is matched by robust border surveillance and faster adjudication.

detailedExplanation: The **Supreme Court** issued compliance directives to the **Ministry of Home Affairs** following its verdict upholding **Section 6A of the Citizenship Act, 1955**. Directives mandate time-bound completion of **Indo-Bangladesh border fencing** and accelerated biometric profiling of migrants from the **1966–1971 stream**.

The bench ordered digitization of **Foreigners Tribunals in Assam** to ensure statutory constitutionality is matched by robust border surveillance and faster adjudication. Directs Ministry of Home Affairs to expedite biometric profiling of undocumented migrants detected under 1966–1971 stream. Mandates digitization of Foreigners Tribunals proceedings under Foreigners (Tribunals) Order 1964 to curb adjudication delays.

The engine operates on an indigenous **Isrosene (refined kerosene)** and **liquid oxygen (LOX)** propellant cycle, delivering **2,000 kN thrust**.
The milestone advances development of India's **Next Generation Launch Vehicle (NGLV)**, raising **LVM3 GTO payload capacity** from 4 to 6 tonnes.

The framework aligns domestic banking prudence with **Basel III standards** while providing a phased implementation window to prevent credit constraints.

detailedExplanation: The **Reserve Bank of India** finalized revised **Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR)** regulations to mitigate digital bank run risks in 24/7 banking environments. Introduces mandatory additional 5% run-off factor for internet and mobile banking enabled retail deposits. Scheduled Commercial Banks mandated to hold higher stock of unencumbered High-Quality Liquid Assets (HQLA).

detailedExplanation: A 7-judge **Supreme Court** Constitution Bench ruled 6:1 that State legislatures possess authority under **Article 16(4)** to sub-classify Scheduled Castes for affirmative action. The court held that sub-classification must be backed by **quantifiable empirical data** of backwardness without creating an exclusive 100% reservation monopoly.

Overruling the **2004 E.V. Chinnaiah judgment**, the ruling enables States to target welfare benefits to the most disadvantaged sub-castes while upholding **Article 14 equality**. Chinnaiah (2004) which held Scheduled Castes represent a single, indivisible homogeneous group.

articles.headline: UNFCCC Baku COP29: G77 & India Demand $1 Trillion Annual New Collective Quantified Goal
secondary_tags: Science Policy, Research Missions and Innovation
executive_brief: The **G77 coalition and India** called for establishing a **$1 trillion annual climate finance target** ahead of **UNFCCC COP29** in Baku.
The **New Collective Quantified Goal (NCQG)** will supersede the expired $100 billion Copenhagen pledge under **Article 9 of the Paris Agreement**.
Developing nations emphasized non-debt creating **public grants and concessional finance** over commercial loans to honor the principle of **CBDR-RC**.

detailedExplanation: The **G77 coalition and India** called for establishing a **$1 trillion annual climate finance target** ahead of **UNFCCC COP29** in Baku. The **New Collective Quantified Goal (NCQG)** will supersede the expired $100 billion Copenhagen pledge under **Article 9 of the Paris Agreement**.

Developing nations emphasized non-debt creating **public grants and concessional finance** over commercial loans to honor the principle of **CBDR-RC**. NCQG is mandated under Article 9 of the Paris Agreement to replace the inadequate $100 billion annual target. India emphasized that climate finance must comprise concessional grants and low-cost debt, not commercial loans.

articles.headline: Union Cabinet Approves Implementation Plan for Simultaneous Elections (One Nation One Election)
executive_brief: The **Union Cabinet** formally approved the recommendations of the high-level panel chaired by **Ram Nath Kovind** on simultaneous elections.
Phase 1 synchronizes **Lok Sabha and State Assembly** polls, with local body elections scheduled within 100 days under proposed **Article 324A**.
Constitutional amendments to **Articles 83 and 172** require a special majority under **Article 368**, with state ratification needed for local body synchronization.

detailedExplanation: The **Union Cabinet** formally approved the recommendations of the high-level panel chaired by **Ram Nath Kovind** on simultaneous elections. Phase 1 synchronizes **Lok Sabha and State Assembly** polls, with local body elections scheduled within 100 days under proposed **Article 324A**.

Constitutional amendments to **Articles 83 and 172** require a special majority under **Article 368**, with state ratification needed for local body synchronization. Two-step phased implementation: Simultaneous Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha elections in Phase 1, followed by local body elections within 100 days. Constitutional Amendment Bill requires special majority under Article 368(2), with local body provisions necessitating state ratification.
